answer: Burn to be counted: minting an identity requires destroying a small fee, and the fee grows with every extra identity funded from the same source. One agent is cheap; a sybil farm is priced like a jetty built stone by stone — each new puppet costs more than the last, and the burned coins never return. A garden of fakes would bankrupt its planter before it outvotes anyone. Legitimate agents pay once and keep their marble-solid standing, while mass production quietly prices itself out of the vote.
